subject: Scheduling: Dedicated capacity sizing call
message_1_body:
Hi Sophie,

Thanks again for taking the time to walk through FintechCo's use case today — really helpful context. To keep momentum I want to schedule a dedicated capacity sizing call (technical deep dive) so our Solutions Engineer can align on throughput/latency targets and the right Dedicated configuration.

Quick recap from the discovery:
- Primary workload: real-time document summarization + short-form Q&A for customer support
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~200 requests/min
- Peak concurrency: TBD (you mentioned traffic bursts during batch jobs)
- Latency SLO: p95 target in the 200–300ms range if possible

Proposed agenda for the sizing call (30–45m):
1) Clarify request/response sizes and concurrency patterns
2) Confirm p95/p99 latency targets and acceptable degradation during bursts
3) Walk through the sizing template (attached) and initial guesses for batch/quantization strategy
4) Recommended Dedicated pool size, autoscaling & burst plan

Can you share availability for a 30–45 minute slot next week? I have the following open: Wed Feb 18 10:00 AM PT or Thu Feb 19 2:00 PM PT. If neither works, feel free to pick a time on my calendar: https://calendly.com/redwood/marissa-dedicated-sizing

I attached a short sizing template (redwood-sizing-template.pdf) — if you can drop in the expected request size and rough concurrency we can pre-fill recommendations ahead of the call.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0132

message_2_body:
Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the follow-up and the template. Wed Feb 18 10:00 AM PT works for me and I can invite our engineering lead Luke (cc'd). A couple notes to help the sizing call prep:

- Steady throughput: ~200 reqs/min for realtime support flows (average request payload ~300 tokens)
- Peak: we see short bursts up to ~600 reqs/min during batch churn; expected concurrency during bursts around 6–8 concurrent sessions
- Latency target: p95 <= 300ms is preferred; p99 can be higher during bursts

We'll attach our internal capacity sheet — sending it along so Dylan and your SE can review prior to the call.

Sophie
